notes: Six praśnas, 67 mantras: the questions of six seekers and the answers of Pippalāda. Meanings and translation follow Śaṅkara's bhāṣya.

sanskrit.deva:
ॐ भद्रं कर्णेभिः शृणुयाम देवा भद्रं पश्येमाक्षभिर्यजत्राः ।
स्थिरैरङ्गैस्तुष्टुवांसस्तनूभिर्व्यशेम देवहितं यदायुः ॥
स्वस्ति न इन्द्रो वृद्धश्रवाः स्वस्ति नः पूषा विश्ववेदाः ।
स्वस्ति नस्तार्क्ष्यो अरिष्टनेमिः स्वस्ति नो बृहस्पतिर्दधातु ॥
ॐ शान्तिः शान्तिः शान्तिः ॥

words.meaning: O you who are worthy of worship

grammar.en: past active participle m. nom. pl.

invocation.translation: Om. May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O you who are worthy of worship. Praising you with firm limbs and bodies, may we attain the life that the gods have appointed. May Indra of great fame grant us well-being; may Pūṣan who knows all grant us well-being; may Tārkṣya of the unharmed wheel-rim grant us well-being; may Bṛhaspati grant us well-being. Om. Peace, peace, peace.
notes: The peace invocation of the Upaniṣads of the Atharvaveda, printed at the opening of the edition. Śaṅkara's Praśna bhāṣya does not comment on it; the translation gives the plain sense of the words.

sanskrit.deva: सुकेशा च भारद्वाजः शैब्यश्च सत्यकामः सौर्यायणी च गार्ग्यः कौसल्यश्चाश्वलायनो भार्गवो वैदर्भिः कबन्धी कात्यायनस्ते हैते ब्रह्मपरा ब्रह्मनिष्ठा परं ब्रह्मान्वेषमाणा एष ह वै तत्सर्वं वक्ष्यतीति ते ह समित्पाणयो भगवन्तं पिप्पलादमुपसन्नाः ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast: sukeśā ca bhāradvājaḥ śaibyaś ca satyakāmaḥ sauryāyaṇī ca gārgyaḥ kausalyaś cāśvalāyano bhārgavo vaidarbhiḥ kabandhī kātyāyanas te haite brahmaparā brahmaniṣṭhā paraṃ brahmānveṣamāṇā eṣa ha vai tatsarvaṃ vakṣyatīti te ha samitpāṇayo bhagavantaṃ pippalādam upasannāḥ || 1 ||

lines.iast: sukeśā ca bhāradvājaḥ śaibyaś ca satyakāmaḥ sauryāyaṇī ca gārgyaḥ kausalyaś cāśvalāyano bhārgavo vaidarbhiḥ kabandhī kātyāyanas te haite brahmaparā brahmaniṣṭhā paraṃ brahmānveṣamāṇā eṣa ha vai tatsarvaṃ vakṣyatīti te ha samitpāṇayo bhagavantaṃ pippalādam upasannāḥ
lines.deva: सुकेशा च भारद्वाजः शैब्यश्च सत्यकामः सौर्यायणी च गार्ग्यः कौसल्यश्चाश्वलायनो भार्गवो वैदर्भिः कबन्धी कात्यायनस्ते हैते ब्रह्मपरा ब्रह्मनिष्ठा परं ब्रह्मान्वेषमाणा एष ह वै तत्सर्वं वक्ष्यतीति ते ह समित्पाणयो भगवन्तं पिप्पलादमुपसन्नाः

padaccheda.iast: sukeśā ca bhāradvājaḥ śaibyaḥ ca satyakāmaḥ sauryāyaṇī ca gārgyaḥ kausalyaḥ ca āśvalāyanaḥ bhārgavaḥ vaidarbhiḥ kabandhī kātyāyanaḥ te ha ete brahma-parāḥ brahma-niṣṭhāḥ param brahma anveṣamāṇāḥ eṣaḥ ha vai tat sarvam vakṣyati iti te ha samit-pāṇayaḥ bhagavantam pippalādam upasannāḥ
padaccheda.deva: सुकेशा च भारद्वाजः शैब्यः च सत्यकामः सौर्यायणी च गार्ग्यः कौसल्यः च आश्वलायनः भार्गवः वैदर्भिः कबन्धी कात्यायनः ते ह एते ब्रह्म-पराः ब्रह्म-निष्ठाः परम् ब्रह्म अन्वेषमाणाः एषः ह वै तत् सर्वम् वक्ष्यति इति ते ह समित्-पाणयः भगवन्तम् पिप्पलादम् उपसन्नाः

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: Sukeśan Bhāradvāja, Satyakāma Śaibya, Sauryāyaṇin Gārgya, Kausalya Āśvalāyana, Bhārgava Vaidarbhi and Kabandhin Kātyāyana: these, intent on (the lower) Brahman and steadfast in it, seeking the supreme Brahman, thought ‘he will tell us all that’, and with fuel in hand they approached the venerable Pippalāda.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the Upaniṣad: this Brāhmaṇa is begun as restating at length what the mantra has said. The story of the seers' questions and the answers is there to praise the knowledge: it is to be received by those who have lived a year with the teacher in brahmacarya and the like, and to be taught by teachers who, like Pippalāda, are all but omniscient, not by anyone whatever. And since it points to brahmacarya and the other means, these are to be practised.

Śaṅkara: Sukeśan by name, the son of Bharadvāja; Satyakāma by name, the son of Śibi; Sauryāyaṇin, the son of Sūrya's son (sauryāyaṇī is a Vedic form for sauryāyaṇiḥ), of the line of Garga; Kausalya by name, the son of Aśvala; Bhārgava, of the line of Bhṛgu, born in Vidarbha; Kabandhin by name, the young descendant of Katya, the form being used of one whose great-grandfather is living.

Śaṅkara: brahmaparāḥ: they had taken the lower Brahman for the highest; brahmaniṣṭhāḥ: they were given to its practice. Seeking the supreme Brahman, that which is eternal and to be known, and resolved to strive for it as they wished, they went to the teacher to learn it.

sanskrit.deva:
तान्ह स ऋषिरुवाच ।
भूय एव तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया संवत्सरं संवत्स्यथ ।
यथाकामं प्रश्नान्पृच्छत ।
यदि विज्ञास्यामः सर्वं ह वो वक्ष्याम इति ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tān ha sa ṛṣir uvāca |
bhūya eva tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śraddhayā saṃvatsaraṃ saṃvatsyatha |
yathākāmaṃ praśnān pṛcchata |
yadi vijñāsyāmaḥ sarvaṃ ha vo vakṣyāma iti || 2 ||

lines.iast: tān ha sa ṛṣir uvāca
bhūya eva tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śraddhayā saṃvatsaraṃ saṃvatsyatha
lines.deva: भूय एव तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया संवत्सरं संवत्स्यथ

lines.iast: yathākāmaṃ praśnān pṛcchata
yadi vijñāsyāmaḥ sarvaṃ ha vo vakṣyāma iti
lines.deva: यदि विज्ञास्यामः सर्वं ह वो वक्ष्याम इति

padaccheda.iast: tān ha saḥ ṛṣiḥ uvāca bhūyaḥ eva tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śraddhayā saṃvatsaram saṃvatsyatha yathā-kāmam praśnān pṛcchata yadi vijñāsyāmaḥ sarvam ha vaḥ vakṣyāmaḥ iti
padaccheda.deva: तान् ह सः ऋषिः उवाच भूयः एव तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया संवत्सरम् संवत्स्यथ यथा-कामम् प्रश्नान् पृच्छत यदि विज्ञास्यामः सर्वम् ह वः वक्ष्यामः इति

translations.text: The seer said to them: ‘Dwell here a year more, with austerity, brahmacarya and faith. Then ask questions as you wish. If we know, we shall tell you all.’

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘again’: though you are ascetics already. tapas is restraint of the senses; here brahmacarya above all; śraddhā is the conviction that it is so, with reverence. ‘Dwell’: intent on serving the teacher well. ‘As you wish’: each on the matter he wishes to know. The word ‘if’ shows the absence of pride, not ignorance or doubt, as is plain from his settling the questions.

sanskrit.deva:
अथ कबन्धी कात्यायन उपेत्य पप्रच्छ ।
भगवन्कुतो ह वा इमाः प्रजाः प्रजायन्त इति ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
atha kabandhī kātyāyana upetya papraccha |
bhagavan kuto ha vā imāḥ prajāḥ prajāyanta iti || 3 ||

lines.iast: atha kabandhī kātyāyana upetya papraccha
bhagavan kuto ha vā imāḥ prajāḥ prajāyanta iti
lines.deva: भगवन्कुतो ह वा इमाः प्रजाः प्रजायन्त इति

padaccheda.iast: atha kabandhī kātyāyanaḥ upetya papraccha bhagavan kutaḥ ha vai imāḥ prajāḥ prajāyante iti
padaccheda.deva: अथ कबन्धी कात्यायनः उपेत्य पप्रच्छ भगवन् कुतः ह वै इमाः प्रजाः प्रजायन्ते इति

translations.text: Then (after the year) Kabandhin Kātyāyana approached and asked: ‘Venerable sir, from where are these creatures born?’

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘then’: after the year. The creatures are brāhmaṇas and the rest. The question is asked so that the effect of the lower knowledge and of action combined, and the course they lead to, may be told.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मै स होवाच ।
प्रजाकामो वै प्रजापतिः ।
स तपोऽतप्यत ।
स तपस्तप्त्वा स मिथुनमुत्पादयते रयिं च प्राणं चेति ।
एतौ मे बहुधा प्रजाः करिष्यत इति ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmai sa hovāca |
prajākāmo vai prajāpatiḥ |
sa tapo 'tapyata |
sa tapas taptvā sa mithunam utpādayate rayiṃ ca prāṇaṃ ceti |
etau me bahudhā prajāḥ kariṣyata iti || 4 ||

lines.iast: tasmai sa hovāca
prajākāmo vai prajāpatiḥ
sa tapo 'tapyata
sa tapas taptvā sa mithunam utpādayate rayiṃ ca prāṇaṃ ceti
lines.deva: स तपस्तप्त्वा स मिथुनमुत्पादयते रयिं च प्राणं चेति

lines.iast: etau me bahudhā prajāḥ kariṣyata iti
lines.deva: एतौ मे बहुधा प्रजाः करिष्यत इति

padaccheda.iast: tasmai saḥ ha uvāca prajā-kāmaḥ vai prajāpatiḥ saḥ tapaḥ atapyata saḥ tapaḥ taptvā saḥ mithunam utpādayate rayim ca prāṇam ca iti etau me bahudhā prajāḥ kariṣyataḥ iti
padaccheda.deva: तस्मै सः ह उवाच प्रजा-कामः वै प्रजापतिः सः तपः अतप्यत सः तपः तप्त्वा सः मिथुनम् उत्पादयते रयिम् च प्राणम् च इति एतौ मे बहुधा प्रजाः करिष्यतः इति

translations.text: He said to him: ‘Prajāpati, desiring offspring, reflected (on the knowledge of the Veda). Having reflected, he produced a pair, food and prāṇa, thinking: these two will make creatures for me in many ways.’

notes: Śaṅkara: Prajāpati: he who, with the knowledge ‘being the Self of all, I shall create the world’ and acting on it, filled with that thought, came to be at the beginning of the kalpa as Hiraṇyagarbha, the lord of the creatures to be created, moving and unmoving. tapas: he reflected on the knowledge cultivated in an earlier birth, whose object is what the Veda reveals. The pair is the means of creation: rayi is Soma, food; prāṇa is Agni, the eater. Thinking so, he made the sun and the moon, in the order in which the world-egg arose.
The e-text reads bahudhāḥ; it is set right here to bahudhā, as the bhāṣya has it.

sanskrit.deva:
आदित्यो ह वै प्राणो रयिरेव चन्द्रमाः ।
रयिर्वा एतत्सर्वं यन्मूर्तं चामूर्तं च ।
तस्मान्मूर्तिरेव रयिः ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ādityo ha vai prāṇo rayir eva candramāḥ |
rayir vā etat sarvaṃ yanmūrtaṃ cāmūrtaṃ ca |
tasmān mūrtir eva rayiḥ || 5 ||

lines.iast: ādityo ha vai prāṇo rayir eva candramāḥ
lines.deva: आदित्यो ह वै प्राणो रयिरेव चन्द्रमाः

lines.iast: rayir vā etat sarvaṃ yanmūrtaṃ cāmūrtaṃ ca
tasmān mūrtir eva rayiḥ

padaccheda.iast: ādityaḥ ha vai prāṇaḥ rayiḥ eva candramāḥ rayiḥ vai etat sarvam yat mūrtam ca amūrtam ca tasmāt mūrtiḥ eva rayiḥ
padaccheda.deva: आदित्यः ह वै प्राणः रयिः एव चन्द्रमाः रयिः वै एतत् सर्वम् यत् मूर्तम् च अमूर्तम् च तस्मात् मूर्तिः एव रयिः

translations.text: The sun is prāṇa; the moon is food. All this is food, what has form and what is formless; therefore (when the two are set apart) form itself is food.

notes: Śaṅkara: the sun is prāṇa, the eater, fire; the moon is rayi, food, Soma. This is one thing, eater and food: Prajāpati is one and yet a pair, the difference being made by what is chief and what is subordinate. All this, the gross with form and the subtle without form, in the shape of eater and food, is rayi. So when the two are set apart, what is other than the formless, that is, form, is rayi, because it is eaten by the formless.
Śaṅkara, going on to the next mantra: so too the formless prāṇa, the eater, is everything, even what is eaten. How?

sanskrit.deva:
अथादित्य उदयन्यत्प्राचीं दिशं प्रविशति तेन प्राच्यान्प्राणान्रश्मिषु संनिधत्ते ।
यद्दक्षिणां यत्प्रतीचीं यदुदीचीं यदधो यदूर्ध्वं यदन्तरा दिशो यत्सर्वं प्रकाशयति तेन सर्वान्प्राणान्रश्मिषु संनिधत्ते ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
athāditya udayan yatprācīṃ diśaṃ praviśati tena prācyān prāṇān raśmiṣu saṃnidhatte |
yad dakṣiṇāṃ yat pratīcīṃ yad udīcīṃ yad adho yad ūrdhvaṃ yad antarā diśo yat sarvaṃ prakāśayati tena sarvān prāṇān raśmiṣu saṃnidhatte || 6 ||

lines.iast: athāditya udayan yatprācīṃ diśaṃ praviśati tena prācyān prāṇān raśmiṣu saṃnidhatte
lines.deva: अथादित्य उदयन्यत्प्राचीं दिशं प्रविशति तेन प्राच्यान्प्राणान्रश्मिषु संनिधत्ते

lines.iast: yad dakṣiṇāṃ yat pratīcīṃ yad udīcīṃ yad adho yad ūrdhvaṃ yad antarā diśo yat sarvaṃ prakāśayati tena sarvān prāṇān raśmiṣu saṃnidhatte
lines.deva: यद्दक्षिणां यत्प्रतीचीं यदुदीचीं यदधो यदूर्ध्वं यदन्तरा दिशो यत्सर्वं प्रकाशयति तेन सर्वान्प्राणान्रश्मिषु संनिधत्ते

padaccheda.iast: atha ādityaḥ udayan yat prācīm diśam praviśati tena prācyān prāṇān raśmiṣu saṃnidhatte yat dakṣiṇām yat pratīcīm yat udīcīm yat adhaḥ yat ūrdhvam yat antarā diśaḥ yat sarvam prakāśayati tena sarvān prāṇān raśmiṣu saṃnidhatte
padaccheda.deva: अथ आदित्यः उदयन् यत् प्राचीम् दिशम् प्रविशति तेन प्राच्यान् प्राणान् रश्मिषु संनिधत्ते यत् दक्षिणाम् यत् प्रतीचीम् यत् उदीचीम् यत् अधः यत् ऊर्ध्वम् यत् अन्तरा दिशः यत् सर्वम् प्रकाशयति तेन सर्वान् प्राणान् रश्मिषु संनिधत्ते

translations.text: Now when the sun, rising, enters the eastern quarter, he thereby takes the living things of the east into his rays. When he enters the southern, the western, the northern, below, above and the quarters between, when he illumines all, he thereby takes all living things into his rays.

notes: Śaṅkara: ‘rising’: coming within sight of living things. ‘Enters’: pervades with his own light. By that pervading he places the living things (prāṇān: prāṇinaḥ) in his rays, which are his own shining and pervade all: that is, he makes them his own self. The quarters between are the corner quarters.
The e-text reads yad dakṣiṇaṃ; it is set right here to dakṣiṇāṃ, as the bhāṣya has it.

तदेतदृचाभ्युक्तम् ॥ ७ ॥

translations.text: He, this Vaiśvānara of all forms, prāṇa, fire, rises. This same thing is declared by a verse:

notes: Śaṅkara: he, the eater, prāṇa, is Vaiśvānara, the Self of all, and of all forms because he is the Self of the universe; as prāṇa and fire, that same eater rises every day, making all the quarters his own.
The e-text reads tad etad dacābhyuktam; it is set right here to ṛcābhyuktam, as the bhāṣya has it.

सहस्ररश्मिः शतधा वर्तमानः प्राणः प्रजानामुदयत्येष सूर्यः ॥ ८ ॥

sahasraraśmiḥ śatadhā vartamānaḥ prāṇaḥ prajānām udayaty eṣa sūryaḥ || 8 ||

lines.deva: विश्वरूपं हरिणं जातवेदसं परायणं ज्योतिरेकं तपन्तम्

lines.deva: सहस्ररश्मिः शतधा वर्तमानः प्राणः प्रजानामुदयत्येष सूर्यः

padaccheda.deva: विश्व-रूपम् हरिणम् जातवेदसम् परायणम् ज्योतिः एकम् तपन्तम् सहस्र-रश्मिः शतधा वर्तमानः प्राणः प्रजानाम् उदयति एषः सूर्यः

translations.text: (The wise have known him,) of all forms, rayed, all-knowing, the final resort, the one light, giving heat. Of a thousand rays, existing in a hundred ways, the life of creatures, this sun rises.

notes: Śaṅkara: hariṇam: having rays. jātavedasam: in whom knowledge has arisen. parāyaṇam: the resting place of all life. ‘The one light’: the eye of all living things, without a second. ‘The wise, the knowers of Brahman, have known the sun as their own Self’ is to be supplied. ‘In a hundred ways’: in many ways, by the difference of living things.
Śaṅkara, going on to the next mantra: the moon, which is form and food, and the sun, which is formless, prāṇa, the eater, are one pair, and it is all. How will the pair make creatures?

तस्यायने दक्षिणं चोत्तरं च ।
तद्ये ह वै तदिष्टापूर्ते कृतमित्युपासते ते चान्द्रमसमेव लोकमभिजयन्ते ।
त एव पुनरावर्तन्ते ।
तस्मादेत ऋषयः प्रजाकामा दक्षिणं प्रतिपद्यन्ते ।
एष ह वै रयिर्यः पितृयाणः ॥ ९ ॥

words.meaning: sacrifice and works of public good

grammar.en: past passive participle n. acc. sg.

translations.text: The year is Prajāpati. It has two paths, the southern and the northern. Those who devote themselves to sacrifice and works of public good, to what is made, win only the world of the moon; they return again. Therefore these seers who desire offspring attain the southern. This path of the fathers is food.

notes: Śaṅkara: that same pair is time: the year is Prajāpati because it is brought about by the pair, for the year is the sum of the lunar days and of the days and nights that moon and sun bring about; not being other than them, it too is the pair of rayi and prāṇa. Its two paths are the two well-known courses of six months each, by which the sun goes south and north, ordaining the worlds of those who do rites alone and of those whose rites are joined with knowledge.

Śaṅkara: the second tat is an adverb. They devote themselves only to what is made (kṛta), sacrifice and works, not to the unmade, the eternal. They win the world of the moon, the part of Prajāpati that is rayi, food, and when what was made is used up they return from there: ‘they enter this world or a lower one’ (Muṇḍaka 1.2.10). Since by sacrifice and works they bring about as their fruit the moon, Prajāpati as food, these seers, seers of heaven, householders who want offspring, reach what they themselves have made: the southern, that is, the moon, marked by the southern course. This rayi, food, is what is marked by the path of the fathers.
The e-text reads kṛtim ity upāsate; it is set right here to kṛtam, as the bhāṣya has it.

sanskrit.deva:
अथोत्तरेण तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया विद्ययात्मानमन्विष्यादित्यमभिजयन्ते ।
एतद्वै प्राणानामायतनमेतदमृतमभयमेतत्परायणम् ।
एतस्मान्न पुनरावर्तन्त इति ।
एष निरोधः ।
तदेष श्लोकः ॥ १० ॥

padaccheda.iast: atha uttareṇa tapasā brahmacaryeṇa śraddhayā vidyayā ātmānam anviṣya ādityam abhijayante etat vai prāṇānām āyatanam etat amṛtam abhayam etat parāyaṇam etasmāt na punaḥ āvartante iti eṣaḥ nirodhaḥ tat eṣaḥ ślokaḥ
padaccheda.deva: अथ उत्तरेण तपसा ब्रह्मचर्येण श्रद्धया विद्यया आत्मानम् अन्विष्य आदित्यम् अभिजयन्ते एतत् वै प्राणानाम् आयतनम् एतत् अमृतम् अभयम् एतत् परायणम् एतस्मात् न पुनः आवर्तन्ते इति एषः निरोधः तत् एषः श्लोकः

translations.text: But by the northern (path), having sought the Self by austerity, brahmacarya, faith and knowledge, they win the sun. This is the abode of all life; this is immortal, free of fear; this is the final goal. From this they do not return. This is the barrier (for those who do not know). On this there is this verse:

notes: Śaṅkara: by the northern course they win the sun, the part of Prajāpati that is prāṇa, the eater. tapas is the conquest of the senses; vidyā is the knowledge whose object is the Self as Prajāpati. Seeking the Self, that is, prāṇa, the sun, the Self of what moves and what stands, and knowing ‘I am he’, they reach the sun. It is the common abode of all the breaths; immortal, imperishable; and so free of fear, not subject to the fear of waning and waxing as the moon is. It is the final goal of those who have knowledge and of those who do rites with knowledge. They do not return from it as those who do rites alone return.

Śaṅkara: nirodha: this is the barrier for those who do not know. They are shut out from the sun: they do not reach the year, the sun, the Self, prāṇa. For the year, whose Self is time, is the barrier of those who do not know.
The e-text reads etad amṛtam ayam etat; it is set right here to abhayam, as the bhāṣya has it.

अथेमे अन्य उ परे विचक्षणं सप्तचक्रे षडर आहुरर्पितमिति ॥ ११ ॥

grammar.en: past passive participle n. acc. sg.

translations.text: They call him the father, five-footed, of twelve forms, rich in water, in the region above heaven. And these others call him the all-seeing, and say that (all this world) is fixed in him, the seven-wheeled, the six-spoked.

notes: Śaṅkara: the five feet are the five seasons, hemanta and śiśira being taken as one: with them, as with feet, the sun, whose Self is the year, goes round. ‘Father’, because he begets all. The twelve forms are the twelve months, his parts. ‘Above heaven’: in the place higher than the world of heaven, that is, in the third heaven. purīṣiṇam: having water. So those who know time say.

Śaṅkara: other knowers of time call that same one vicakṣaṇa, skilled, all-knowing, and say that all this world is fixed, like the spokes in the nave of a wheel, in him whose Self is time, ever moving, seven-wheeled in the form of the seven horses, and six-spoked, having six seasons. Whether as five-footed and of twelve forms, or as seven-wheeled and six-spoked, the year, time, Prajāpati, marked by moon and sun, is the cause of the world.
The e-text reads dvādaśakṛtiṃ; it is set right here to dvādaśākṛtiṃ, as the bhāṣya has it.

तस्य कृष्णपक्ष एव रयिः शुक्लः प्राणः ।
तस्मादेत ऋषयः शुक्ल इष्टं कुर्वन्तीतर इतरस्मिन् ॥ १२ ॥

tasya kṛṣṇapakṣa eva rayiḥ śuklaḥ prāṇaḥ

translations.text: The month is Prajāpati. Its dark fortnight is food, its bright fortnight prāṇa. Therefore these seers perform their sacrifice in the bright fortnight, the others in the other.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: that same Prajāpati called the year, in whom all this is woven, is wholly contained in his own part, the month.

Śaṅkara: the month too is a pair as described. One part of it, the dark fortnight, is rayi, food, the moon; the other, the bright fortnight, is prāṇa, the sun, the eater, fire. Since these seers, who see prāṇa, see everything as prāṇa, the bright fortnight, they sacrifice in the bright fortnight even when they sacrifice in the dark one, for apart from prāṇa they see no dark fortnight. The others do not see prāṇa; they see only the dark, whose mark is not seeing, and they sacrifice in the other, the dark fortnight, even when they do so in the bright.
In the e-text the sentence of the bhāṣya that introduces the mantra stands in the mūla; it is removed here.

sanskrit.deva:
अहोरात्रो वै प्रजापतिः ।
तस्याहरेव प्राणो रात्रिरेव रयिः ।
प्राणं वा एते प्रस्कन्दन्ति ये दिवा रत्या संयुज्यन्ते ।
ब्रह्मचर्यमेव तद्यद्रात्रौ रत्या संयुज्यन्ते ॥ १३ ॥

prāṇaṃ vā ete praskandanti ye divā ratyā saṃyujyante

padaccheda.deva: अहोरात्रः वै प्रजापतिः तस्य अहः एव प्राणः रात्रिः एव रयिः प्राणम् वै एते प्रस्कन्दन्ति ये दिवा रत्या संयुज्यन्ते ब्रह्मचर्यम् एव तत् यत् रात्रौ रत्या संयुज्यन्ते

translations.text: Day and night are Prajāpati. Of it day is prāṇa and night is food. They waste their prāṇa who unite in love by day; that they unite in love by night is brahmacarya itself.

notes: Śaṅkara: that Prajāpati who is the month is in turn contained in his own part, the day and night. praskandanti: they drive out, or dry up, the prāṇa that is the day, cutting it off from themselves. ratyā: with a woman, the cause of pleasure. Those who do so are fools; so it is not to be done: this is a prohibition made in passing. That they unite at night, in season, is brahmacarya, because it is commended: so going to one's wife in season is to be done; this too is an injunction made in passing. The matter in hand is this: that Prajāpati who is day and night abides as food, rice, barley and the rest.

lines.deva: अन्नं वै प्रजापतिस्ततो ह वै तद्रेतः

lines.iast: tasmād imāḥ prajāḥ prajāyanta iti

padaccheda.iast: annam vai prajāpatiḥ tataḥ ha vai tat retaḥ tasmāt imāḥ prajāḥ prajāyante iti
padaccheda.deva: अन्नम् वै प्रजापतिः ततः ह वै तत् रेतः तस्मात् इमाः प्रजाः प्रजायन्ते इति

translations.text: Food is Prajāpati. From it comes seed, and from that these creatures are born.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: having changed in this order,

Śaṅkara: from food comes seed, the seed of man, the cause of offspring; from that, shed in a woman, these creatures, men and the rest, are born. So the question ‘from where are creatures born?’ is settled: in the order that begins with the pair of moon and sun and ends with day and night, through food, blood and seed, these creatures are born.

sanskrit.deva:
तद्ये ह वै तत्प्रजापतिव्रतं चरन्ति ।
ते मिथुनमुत्पादयन्ते ।
तेषामेवैष ब्रह्मलोकः ।
येषां तपो ब्रह्मचर्यं ।
येषु सत्यं प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥ १५ ॥

padaccheda.deva: तत् ये ह वै तत् प्रजापति-व्रतम् चरन्ति ते मिथुनम् उत्पादयन्ते तेषाम् एव एषः ब्रह्म-लोकः येषाम् तपः ब्रह्मचर्यम् येषु सत्यम् प्रतिष्ठितम्

grammar.en: past passive participle n. nom. sg.

translations.text: That being so, those who observe this vow of Prajāpati produce a pair (a son and a daughter). Theirs alone is this world of Brahmā (the world of the moon) who have austerity and brahmacarya, in whom truth is established.

notes: Śaṅkara: ha and vai are particles that recall what is well known. Those householders who observe the vow of Prajāpati, going to the wife in season, have this seen fruit: they beget a pair, a son and a daughter. And the unseen fruit, for those of them who perform sacrifice, works and gifts, is this world of Brahmā that is the moon's, marked by the path of the fathers: for those who have austerity (the vows of one who has completed his studies and the like) and brahmacarya, and in whom truth, the avoiding of untruth, stands without fail at all times.

Śaṅkara, going on to the next mantra: but the northern course marked by the sun, which is the state of being prāṇa, is stainless, pure, not stained like the moon's world of Brahmā with waxing and waning. Whose is it?

sanskrit.deva: तेषामसौ विरजो ब्रह्मलोको न येषु जिह्ममनृतं न माया चेति ॥ १६ ॥
sanskrit.iast: teṣām asau virajo brahmaloko na yeṣu jihmam anṛtaṃ na māyā ceti || 16 ||

lines.iast: teṣām asau virajo brahmaloko na yeṣu jihmam anṛtaṃ na māyā ceti
lines.deva: तेषामसौ विरजो ब्रह्मलोको न येषु जिह्ममनृतं न माया चेति

padaccheda.iast: teṣām asau virajaḥ brahma-lokaḥ na yeṣu jihmam anṛtam na māyā ca iti
padaccheda.deva: तेषाम् असौ विरजः ब्रह्म-लोकः न येषु जिह्मम् अनृतम् न माया च इति

translations.text: Theirs is that stainless world of Brahmā in whom there is no crookedness, no untruth and no deceit.

notes: Śaṅkara: for householders crookedness cannot be avoided, since their ends require many dealings that conflict with one another; nor untruth, on occasions of play, jest and the like. māyā is to show oneself outwardly in one way and act in another: false conduct. Those entitled in whom these faults are absent, there being no occasion for them, the brahmacārins, forest-dwellers and mendicants, have that stainless world of Brahmā, in keeping with their means. This is the course of those whose rites are joined with knowledge; the world of Brahmā named before, that of the moon, belongs to those who do rites alone.
The e-text reads jihvam; it is set right here to jihmam, as the bhāṣya has it.
